Complete the following tasks using Matplotlib and Seaborn.¶

  • Your task is to replicate the given plots using the penguins data.
  • Plots are in Plots.html.

Task 8: Explain the code and plot.¶

  • Use the given code, no need to change it
  • Figure out, what does correlation mean.
  • Explain the code.
  • Figure out, how to read the heatmap. Why is there always 1 (or 1.00) on the diagonal? What do the colors indicate?

ANSWER TO TASK 8 QUESTIONS:¶

1. CORRILATION:¶
  • Coorelation means there is a relation between the the variables: when one variable changes, it will lead to the change to the other variable in the same direction or opposite direction.
2. EXPLAIN THE CODE:¶
  • See comments in the below Code.
3. HOW TO READ THE HEATMAP:¶

  • The color is associated with the numbers

  • The number is from -1 to +1.

    • The closer to number 1, the more correlated, which means the 2 variables are likely to move together ("Positive Correlation").
    • The closer to 0, the less correlated they are ("No Correlation").
    • The closer to -1, the more correlated, BUT they are moving in an opposite direction ("Negative correlation" or "Inverse correlation").

  • The number 1 on the diagonal is where x = y = same variable, then naturally they move together, since they are the same one variable.

In [ ]:
corr = penguins.select_dtypes("number").corr() # Plot a Correlation table/matrix for all "number" datatype

plt.figure(figsize=(8, 6)) # Define the size of the correlation table

sns.heatmap(            # Create a heatmap in the table, showing the level of correlation with color density.
    corr,
    annot=True, # Plot the numbers in each cell of the table
    cmap="coolwarm",  # color map is coolwarm: red - hot; blue - cool.
    fmt=".2f" # format of numbers with decimal =2.
)

plt.title("Correlation Matrix") # Plot the table with Title "Correlation Matrix"

plt.show() # Show the table
